sources.entry: Telegraf | Server agent for collecting and reporting metrics

summary.one_liner: Telegraf is a plugin-driven server agent that collects, processes, aggregates and writes metrics, logs and other data, shipped as a single static binary.
summary.what_it_does: Telegraf runs as an agent that reads data from input plugins at each collection interval and sends it to output plugins at each flush interval. The README says it offers over 300 plugins covering system monitoring, cloud services, messaging, devices, logs, networking, and Windows-specific sources such as Event Log and Performance Counters. Users pick plugins and settings in a TOML configuration file, which is passed to Telegraf at startup. It also supports user-defined code to collect, transform and transmit data. The README describes it as compiling into a standalone static binary with no external dependencies.
use_cases: collect server CPU, memory, disk and network metrics
gather Docker and Nvidia GPU stats
poll SNMP, Modbus or OPC UA devices
forward metrics to Kafka, MQTT or AMQP
how_to_run: Install a binary, Docker image, RPM or DEB package (see the install guide linked in the README)
Write a TOML configuration listing the input and output plugins you want
Start Telegraf and pass it the configuration file
notable: Over 300 plugins for inputs, processors, aggregators and outputs
Standalone static binary with no external dependencies
Each plugin has its own README under the plugins directory
caveats: The README points to separate install and configuration guides rather than giving full setup steps
Community support is via Slack or forums; GitHub issues are limited to bugs and feature requests
